subject: Food Science
title: Freeze-Drying
description: A quick, practical guide to Freeze-Drying.

hook.text: Freeze-dried strawberries last 25 years and weigh almost nothing. NASA uses them. So do backpackers and soldiers.

buildup.text: Freeze-drying freezes food to -40°C then drops pressure—ice turns directly to vapor without ever becoming liquid.

discovery.text: This process is called sublimation. It removes 98% of water while leaving the food's cellular structure perfectly intact.

twist.text: Add water and freeze-dried food returns to near-original texture. Conventional drying collapses cells permanently.

climax.text: Freeze-drying is expensive—10 times the cost of hot-air drying. Its superior quality justifies it for high-value products.

punchline.text: Skip the liquid phase entirely. Ice becomes vapor and quality stays locked in.

quiz.question: What is sublimation in freeze-drying?
options: Ice turning directly to vapor without passing through liquid
